parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish بهار (bahâr), from Arabic بَهَار (bahār, “spice”), from Classical Persian بَهَار (bahār, “blossom”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish بكار (bekâr, “bachelor”), from Arabic بِكْر (bikr, “virgin”). Historically confused with the homophone بیكار (bekâr, “unemployed”), from Classical Persian بیکَار (bēkār).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish بللور (billur), borrowed from Arabic بِلَّوْر (billawr), borrowed from Classical Persian بِلّور (billōr), from Middle Persian bylwl (/⁠*bēlūr⁠/), borrowed from Pali veḷuriya, from Proto-Dravidian *weḷ-ūr (name of a city) + Pali -iya.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جاموس (camus), from Arabic جَامُوس (jāmūs), from Classical Persian گَامیش (gāmēš). Doublet of kömüş and camış.

parole.significato: gift of the gab, the skill or ability to talk eloquently, glibly, and convincingly
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جربزه (cerbeze), from Arabic جَرْبَزَة (jarbaza, “deception, swindle”), itself possibly from Classical Persian گربز (gorbez, “cunning”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جوهر (cevher), from Arabic جَوْهَر (jawhar), from Classical Persian گوهر (gawhar).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دُسْتُور (düstur). Doublet of destur, borrowed directly from Classical Persian دَسْتُور (dastūr).

parole.significato: science (only referring to biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فن (fen, “kind, variety; art, science”), from Arabic فَنّ (fann), ultimately from Classical Persian پَنْد (pand, “knack, trick”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فنجان (fincan), borrowed from Arabic فِنْجَان (finjān), borrowed from Classical Persian پِنْگَان (pingān), possibly borrowed from Classical Syriac ܦܝܢܟܐ (pīnəḵā), from Aramaic פִּינְכָא (pīnəkā), borrowed from Ancient Greek πίναξ (pínax).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قلندر (kalender), from Arabic قَلَنْدَر (qalandar), from Classical Persian کَلَنْدَر (kalandar).

parole.significato: lilac, any large, flowering shrub of the genus Syringa, especially Syringa vulgaris
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish لیلاق (leylak), from Arabic لَيْلَك (laylak, “lilac”), itself from Classical Persian لِیلَک (līlak, “indigo; lilac”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ملا (mulla, molla), منلا (monla), from Arabic مُلَّا (mullā), from Classical Persian مُلَّا (mullā), from Arabic مَوْلًى (mawlan). Doublet of mevla.

parole.significato: black person of African descent, Negro
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish زنجی (zenci), from Arabic زَنْجِيّ (zanjiyy), from Classical Persian زنگی (zangī).
